services.title: Implants, rehabilitation and cosmetic work in one practice
services.lead: Two treatment pillars: implant dentistry grounded in bone biology research, and aesthetic work planned by a periodontally-trained clinician so the result holds up structurally.

implants.title: Dental implants
implants.description: Single implants, multiple implants or full-arch rehabilitation, planned from digital radiography or a CBCT scan and placed under local anaesthesia.

grafting.title: Bone grafting & sinus lift
grafting.description: Performed when the diagnostic imaging indicates it is needed — a conservative, evidence-based call on grafting and healing timelines rather than a default step.

rehabilitation.title: Oral rehabilitation
rehabilitation.description: Prosthetic restoration after healing: crown, bridge or implant-supported denture, including cases with failing bridgework.

veneers.title: Porcelain veneers
veneers.description: Thin, custom-fabricated shells that correct shape, spacing and colour while preserving as much natural tooth structure as possible.

smileDesign.title: Smile design
smileDesign.description: Digital mock-ups and proportion analysis before any irreversible preparation, so you can preview the result before deciding.

whitening.title: Whitening & restorative aesthetics
whitening.description: In-office and supervised take-home whitening calibrated to a realistic, stable shade, plus tooth-coloured bonding and zirconia crown work matched to adjacent teeth.

services.note: Aesthetic treatment that ignores gum health and bite mechanics tends to age poorly. Dr. Meta has taught in the Department of Periodontology at USAL/AOA since 2008 and is a member of the Argentine Society of Periodontology, so smile design decisions account for gum line, tissue health and long-term stability — not only shade and shape.

about.title: A clinician's background, in detail
about.lead: Credentials matter most when they are verifiable. Below is the clinical, research and teaching record — not a summary.
paragraphs: Since 2007, Dr. Meta has run a private practice in Buenos Aires focused on dental implant placement, oral rehabilitation and general dentistry, with a significant share of English-speaking expatriate patients. Since 2008 he has been the suggested dentist of the U.S. Embassy in Argentina for U.S. citizens and Foreign Service personnel stationed in the country. Over the years he has also treated diplomats from more than 10 countries, an experience that has broadened the cultural perspective he brings to his clinical practice. His office coordinates directly with several major expatriate and international insurance providers, and works alongside two orthodontists for combined treatment plans.

Before opening his practice, Dr. Meta spent three years as a fully-funded graduate researcher at The Ohio State University, where his MS thesis characterized bone phenotypes in the mandibles of high and low bone-mineral-density mice, advised by Dr. Sarandeep Huja. That research produced five peer-reviewed papers in journals including the Journal of Periodontology and Calcified Tissue International, and a further fourteen conference abstracts presented in the U.S. and Argentina between 2000 and 2017 — including a randomized controlled trial on analgesic protocols after dental implant placement, published in Implant Dentistry in 2017. He has served as an ad hoc reviewer for the Journal of Periodontology and Orthodontics and Craniofacial Research.

Dr. Meta taught at the postgraduate level in Buenos Aires from 2003 to 2023. He chaired Oral Implantology Clinics I–III in the MS in Oral Implantology program at USAL/AOA from 2012 to 2021, directed the predoctoral Biophysics program from 2012 to 2016, and held teaching roles in the Department of Periodontology from 2008 to 2015. He has supervised two completed MS theses on guided bone regeneration and served on three additional thesis committees.

In 2008 he translated chapters of Clinical Periodontology and Implant Dentistry (Lindhe, Lang & Karring, 5th edition) from English to Spanish for Editorial Médica Panamericana. He is a member of the Argentine Dental Association (AOA), the Argentine Society of Periodontology (SAP) and the International Association for Dental Research (IADR), and has presented research in both Spanish and English at meetings in Buenos Aires and at Ohio State's Mallory-Coleman Resident Research Day.

process.title: What implant treatment typically involves
process.lead: The sequence below is the standard path. Timelines depend on bone quality and whether grafting is required.

one.title: Diagnostic consultation
one.description: A clinical exam with digital radiography or, in most cases, a CBCT scan to evaluate bone volume and density before any surgical step is planned.

two.title: Treatment planning
two.description: A single implant, multiple implants or full-arch rehabilitation — including bone grafting or a sinus lift when the diagnostic imaging indicates it is needed.

three.title: Placement and healing
three.description: Implant placement under local anaesthesia, followed by the healing and osseointegration period. Pain management follows the evidence from Dr. Meta's own published trial.

four.title: Prosthetic restoration
four.description: Crown, bridge or implant-supported denture. A straightforward single-implant case runs roughly 3 to 6 months from placement to final restoration.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.lead: Real questions international and local patients ask before their first visit.

items.question: Do you speak English fluently, not just basic phrases?
items.answer: Yes. Dr. Meta spent three years as a graduate researcher in Columbus, Ohio, and has treated English-speaking expatriates since 2007 — consultations and treatment planning happen in fluent, clinical English.

items.question: Where exactly is the practice located?
items.answer: The office is at Av. R. Scalabrini Ortiz 2089, 8th floor, Palermo, Buenos Aires (CABA), a central and easily accessible neighbourhood. Directions are in the contact section below.

items.question: Can I book an appointment if I'm only in Buenos Aires for a few days?
items.answer: Yes. Contact the office by email or WhatsApp with your dates and the office will do its best to accommodate short-notice and traveller appointments, including urgent care.

items.question: Do you work directly with international insurance?
items.answer: Yes, with direct coordination for several major expatriate and international insurance providers. For other insurers, the office provides detailed documentation for out-of-network reimbursement.

items.question: Is treatment in Buenos Aires significantly less expensive than in the U.S. or Europe?
items.answer: Costs are generally lower than in the U.S. or Western Europe for comparable implant and cosmetic work, though pricing depends on the specific treatment plan — ask for a written estimate after your diagnostic consultation.

items.question: How is implant treatment planned?
items.answer: With a diagnostic consultation and, in most cases, a CBCT scan to evaluate bone volume and density before any surgical step is planned.

items.question: What is Dr. Meta's background specific to implants?
items.answer: An MS in Oral Biology from Ohio State University with a thesis on bone density and mandibular structure, five related peer-reviewed publications, and a 2017 randomized controlled trial on pain management after implant placement, published in Implant Dentistry. He also taught for more than 10 years in the Oral Implantology department at USAL/AOA and in the Department of Periodontology.

items.question: Can I see what my smile will look like before committing to veneers?
items.answer: Yes, through a digital mock-up and proportion analysis before any irreversible tooth preparation.

items.question: Are veneers permanent?
items.answer: Veneers require some enamel removal and are considered a long-term, not fully reversible, treatment. Dr. Meta will discuss durability and alternatives during your consultation.
